A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAIF research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated content and distinguishing formatting changes.

before.justification: v5 reports original model evaluations, ablations, OOD generalization experiments, and additional instruction-following, general-purpose, and mathematics results in the appendix.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline evaluations on IFBench in Table 5.

M1.justification: Instruction synthesis, rule-centric GRPO rewards, superior-CoT filtering, and behavior cloning remain unchanged. Figure 2's new Self-Instruct terminology describes the procedure already specified in v5 Section 3.2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same instruction and DeepScaleR training data, seven main instruction benchmarks, IFBench OOD evaluation, and appendix general-purpose and mathematics benchmarks. Added IFBench comparators do not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds CoT and self-DeepClaude (SDC) for Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct and Ministral-8B-Instruct, plus SFT for all six backbones. These methods appeared elsewhere in v5 but were absent from its IFBench comparison.

E3.justification: IFBench retains the same backbones and prompt-level/instruction-level strict and loose metrics. Experimental settings in Section 4.1 and Appendices A.2 and A.5 are unchanged; no distinct protocol revision accompanies the added comparators.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 extends the existing OOD robustness analysis to test whether RAIF's advantages over prompting and SFT persist on unseen constraints. The component ablations, training analyses, case studies, and appendix generalization analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged. The additional IFBench rows report point estimates without introducing repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds twelve baseline result rows while preserving all twelve original rows. For example, Qwen2.5-1.5B gains reported CoT, SDC, and SFT averages of 15.67, 17.74, and 18.55; its I/O and RAIF averages remain 17.82 and 19.95. Other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, objectives, reward equations, and Appendix A.1 symbol definitions are unchanged. Differences in equation typography do not alter the mathematics; no new proof or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions, headline 11.74% gain, and OOD generalization claim. The additional IFBench comparisons provide supporting evidence without redefining those core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds explanations for CoT/SDC behavior, attributes SFT generalization difficulties to reasoning-distribution mismatch, and advances a data-efficiency argument. Some statements overgeneralize Table 5: SDC does not outperform CoT on Ministral, and SFT improves Qwen2.5-1.5B. Appendix A.8 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Data-generation prompts, model identities, hyperparameters, hardware, training durations, inference settings, and code/data access information are retained. The 13K complex-instruction count emphasized in the new discussion was already documented in v5.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section are unchanged, but Section 4.4 newly contrasts RAIF's 13K instruction examples with roughly 800K SFT examples attributed to DeepSeek R1. This adds a limited comparative positioning argument, rather than a matched experimental comparison.

P1.justification: v7 adds a localized discussion in Section 4.4, changes UTU Team to Youtu-Agent Team, moves the author-list note into a footnote, and revises Figure 2 terminology. The overall narrative structure and appendix organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 receives new fonts, generic model icons, and revised labels while retaining its workflow. Table 5 expands from twelve to twenty-four rows and moves from page 14 to page 15. Header branding and surrounding pagination also change.

improvement.justification: Table 5 strengthens the OOD evidence by adding prompting and SFT alternatives to v5's I/O-only comparison; RAIF has the highest reported average for each backbone. This is a limited net improvement, tempered by inaccurate new generalizations: Ministral's SDC average is below CoT, and Qwen2.5-1.5B improves under SFT. The 800K-versus-13K argument also lacks a matched data-budget experiment.
